data.exact_reserve_text: An overall improvement of GBP 3.3 million on prior years' provisions was experienced during the year. This is due to improvements of GBP 3.6 million on property reinsurance and GBP 0.2 million on marine reinsurance partially offset by a deterioration of GBP 0.5 million on casualty reinsurance.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Effects of COVID-19 still being felt in 2018 year of account, affected 2019 year of account with associated business interruption claims, and affected multiple years of account including 2020, leading to disappointing performance against initial expectations.

prior_year_events.event_name: Court rulings / legal developments (CG Restaurants & Bars v RSA, Stonegate v MS Amlin)
prior_year_events.impact_description: New court cases expected to challenge claims payment basis, leading to unwelcome development and closure of 2018 year of account with a loss of 20.8% of capacity.

Ongoing legal issues and awaited rulings in Australia affecting business interruption claims, making ultimate liability uncertain and leading to the 2019 year of account remaining open with a forecast loss range of (25%) to (45%).

named_events.loss_description: A very severe winter storm and freeze hit the US state of Texas causing around US$15bn of insured damage.

The largest single loss event, hitting the United States in August 2021 causing an estimated total insured loss of around US$36bn. It was the largest natural perils loss incurred by the syndicate during 2021.
An extremely damaging flood hit central Europe in July which caused around US$13bn of insured damage.
A terrible outbreak of tornadoes across the US Mid-West, occurring 'out of season' in December 2021.
A wildfire in Denver, occurring 'out of season' in December 2021.

data.standardized_narrative: Argenta Syndicate 6134 experienced an overall release of GBP 3.3 million in prior year claims provisions during 2021, representing a 3.09% release against opening gross reserves. This favorable development was primarily driven by improvements in property reinsurance (GBP 3.6 million) and marine reinsurance (GBP 0.2 million), partially offset by a deterioration in casualty reinsurance (GBP 0.5 million). However, the report also noted adverse developments for the 2018 and 2019 years of account, with the 2018 YOA closing at a loss of 20.8% of capacity due to COVID-19 effects and new court cases (CG Restaurants & Bars v RSA, Stonegate v MS Amlin). The 2019 YOA remained open with a forecast loss range of (25%) to (45%) due to COVID-19, business interruption claims, and ongoing legal issues in Australia. The 2020 YOA also performed disappointingly against initial expectations due to COVID-19. The syndicate also faced significant natural catastrophe events in 2021, including Winter Storm Uri, Hurricane Ida, Central Europe floods, US Mid-West tornadoes, and Denver wildfires.

data.data_quality_notes: The narrative on page 3 regarding year of account results (2018, 2019, 2020 YOAs showing losses or disappointing performance) appears to contradict the overall 'improvement of GBP 3.3 million on prior years' provisions' stated on page 10. The GBP 3.3 million figure is taken as the primary prior year development as it is explicitly stated as a movement in provisions. The claims development triangle on page 15, when calculated for prior years (2018, 2019), yields a net strengthening of GBP 2.525 million, which also does not align with the GBP 3.3 million release from the narrative. The narrative figure is prioritized due to its explicit statement of 'overall improvement on prior years' provisions'.
